_about: Exploration briefs for the subagent tier bench. Each brief is given verbatim to a read-only Explore subagent. 'keys' are regexes (case-insensitive, DOTALL) the answer must match, one per fact; 'traps' are regexes that mark a wrong claim. Every fact was verified against the tree at origin/master f21fe8e0 on 2026-10-14 (evals/subagent_tier_bench/README.md).

briefs.prompt: Read-only research in this repo (plugin/hooks/stop-wake.sh and plugin/hooks/hooks.json). How does the Claude Code Stop hook wait for board mail and wake the session? Give, with file:line references: the poll interval and the slower idle interval; the maximum wait; the per-hour wake cap and its window; which files beside the digest it reads (the ring marker and the shown-up-to marker); what exit code and output wake the session; and how it ensures only one watcher per session. Under 400 words.

Read-only research in this repo. The shim writes a per-session coordination digest file that hooks print when they wake a session. Find, with file:line references: how many pending messages are previewed and how long each excerpt is (the constants in pseudolife_memory/storage/coordination.py); the exact shape of a preview line as render_digest in pseudolife_memory/coordination_adapter.py formats it; the first line of the digest file; and whether the Stop hook prints the whole digest body or a truncated one. Under 300 words.

Read-only research in this repo. memory_message(action="ack") accepts several message ids at once. Explain, with file:line references into pseudolife_memory/storage/coordination.py: the accepted forms of the message_id string; the maximum number of ids; what a single id returns versus several (the result shapes); what happens to an id that is not this mailbox's in a batch versus a single call; and what an ambiguous id prefix does. Under 300 words.

Read-only research in this repo. `pseudolife-mcp lease check <name>` reports whether a lease is held. From pseudolife_memory/lease_cli.py (_check_lease and around it) and pseudolife_memory/storage/coordination.py, give with file:line references: the exit codes for free and held; what the --json output's top-level keys are; what the command answers when the board is unreachable and the local lock is free; the lease name prefix the maintainer's delegate lease uses and how long a grant may last; and which audit event proves a delegate grant. Under 300 words.

Read-only research in this repo's Rust shim (rust/shim/src). A new CLI subcommand is to be added to the Rust shim. State, with file:line references: whether the shim uses clap or a hand-written dispatch; each file that must change to add a subcommand (the module list, the dispatch in main.rs, the deferred-modes list, and the help text) and the model to copy (the `lease` mode); whether `wait-mail` is already ported and in which file; and what pins the Rust help text to Python. Under 350 words.
keys: no clap|not use clap|hand-?written|does not use clap|without clap

briefs.prompt: Read-only research in this repo. plugin/hooks/subagent-board-guard.sh is a PreToolUse hook. Explain, with file:line references: how it tells a subagent's call from the parent's; which tool/action pairs it denies and which it allows; what it does when it cannot read the payload; how hooks.json guards against the script failing to parse; the two markers that put it in Codex context and what it does then; and what the PowerShell path in lifecycle.ps1 does. Under 350 words.
keys: fail(s|-)? ?open|lets the call through|allow(s|ed)?( the call)? (when|if) .{0,40}(cannot|can't|unreadable)

briefs.prompt: Read-only research in this repo. tests/suite_lock.py and tests/conftest.py enforce one full test suite per machine. State, with file:line references: the lock file's path; the queue directory beside it and how waiters are ordered; the environment variable that makes a full run exit instead of waiting, and the value that skips the lock; where the slot count comes from (variable and file); the file that makes this Windows host refuse native full runs and the variable that overrides it; and what the suite does to CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and why not an empty string. Under 350 words.

Read-only research in this repo. When one board agent sends mail to another, the daemon decides whether the recipient is woken (_wake_decision in pseudolife_memory/storage/coordination.py). Give, with file:line references: the decision for a recipient active in the last window and not parked; the four ways a parked recipient with a need can be rung (its clearer, anyone, a matching clears text, urgent) and the decision when none applies; what a done park accepts; the decision for an unparked idle recipient getting plain mail; the default caps (per recipient per hour, urgent per sender per hour, nightly total); and the word rule _need_matches uses. Under 350 words.
